- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70% from prior 18d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish events outnumber bearish, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance or add 3–5% upward bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward buffer to forecast mean.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to lag true price movements; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead in time horizon if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7d average if no strong trend.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model overfits to recent highs; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior 18d high unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
